H3b asks only whether one training signal, in one family of small environments, finds the policy Result 10 makes best there. Holding solo skill fixed does not hold skill at coordinating with others fixed. The multi-copy probe describes how agents scale, but cannot separate coordination from reward caps and rivalry, or tell whether an effect works through an intermediate channel.

The bargaining game is a cartoon of bargaining, and I say so. Offers are a small fixed set, and an agreement is just a recorded pair of moves. Enforcement is a switch, not an institution with its own costs and failures. The declining side’s objective is held fixed.

The power shift is scheduled and announced. That removes uncertainty about power, which The War Baseline treats as a second route to war, so that the commitment problem can be studied alone. Raiding is a raid on a tile, and the security dilemma it creates has no diplomacy beyond the bargaining moves.

The planning agents search a simulator they are given, with a learned model of the opponent. No real actor has that foresight. So the planners set an upper bound on what looking ahead can do in these games. A difference between planners and other agents is a result about how agents are built, not about minds.

The security threshold is a property of these games’ exchange and consumption rates. It carries over to no system outside them, except as the claim that such a threshold exists and can be measured.

It tests one idea, not another

This design tests the conjecture that the type of a mind’s aims shapes the type of conflict it enters. It does not test the separate thesis, from Ends, Rank and Conflict, that a mind’s capability does not fix its aims. Whatever the human sample shows about which aims were common among leaders or creators, it cannot show which aims can be installed in a machine.

What would change the picture

The feasibility stage is where the answer could change. Suppose the archive yields at least 420 eligible heirs with usable documents, and simulation at the measured rates puts support power at 0.70 or more. Then H1 would leave the fallback and could be supported as well as lost. If the machines pass H2’s checks in the gates and the reference arm, H2 widens to the whole pool; if any of those checks fails, H2 stays on the 600. Phase 0 replaces the assumed archive yields, base rates, pool counts and coding-error rates in Part 8 with measured ones before the human study is deposited, while unmeasurable counterpart responses are still simulated across a grid.

Part 10. What to take away

Two conditions would make choosing and bounding a machine’s training objective a real lever on the risk of its arrival. The content of a mind’s aims would have to change the conflict it enters, and a training objective would have to fix the aims a learned agent pursues. That remains a conditional claim. The machine side of this design speaks to it only for small sandbox agents, in the settings they were trained in.

The design gives each of six hypotheses a way to lose, and gives the conjecture as a whole no single verdict. It leaves out every illustration that helped form the idea, draws leaders by office rather than fame, and reads aims only from records made before the relevant outcome window opens. It compares heirs who did not choose their moment, tests machine coders against hand-built evidence, and fixes six rules before any confirmatory data are read.

Whether the archive holds enough heirs, and whether the machines pass their checks, are questions to measure, not assume. So the design’s practical conclusion is to fund the feasibility stage first. On the provisional counts, H1 is expected to enter the fallback, where it can still lose against the 2.2 bar but cannot be supported.

Where to read more

  • A Test the Conjecture Could Lose, the technical paper: the full design, with exact definitions, protocols, decision rules, the Lean checks and the computed figures in its appendices and supplement.
  • The War Baseline: the analysis of the commitment problem at a capable machine’s arrival, which this design takes as given.
  • Ends, Rank and Conflict: the conjecture under test, the dimensions of aims, the two layers of atrocity and the historical illustrations left out of the test.
  • Measures That Depend on Ends: the analysis of how training objectives install and bound the aims a machine learns.
  • Changing the Ends: the reading of instrumental convergence that defines the worrying knowledge-with-rival-inputs case, and the one-page sketch of this test.
  • Limits, and an Answer: the stated limit that no source drawn on in the series shows satiable aims can be trained.
